concept.name: Principal component analysis
concept.definition: A linear dimensionality-reduction method that rotates centered features into orthogonal directions ordered by the variance they explain.
concept.intuition: It is a learnable mapping or representation used to turn features into predictions or groups.
concept.mechanics: Center the training matrix, eigendecompose its covariance matrix or apply singular-value decomposition, retain leading components, and project later rows with the fitted loadings.
concept.formula: PC scores = centered X times loading vectors
concept.failure_modes: Flexible models can fit noise, shift under new regimes, and conceal instability when tuning is repeated on the same validation data.
concept.misconceptions: Greater model complexity or in-sample accuracy does not by itself imply better out-of-sample trading results.
concept.example: Three correlated yield features are projected onto a first component explaining 85% of their training variance.
